text:
In the case of Smith v. State Bank, the plaintiff, Ms. Smith, alleges that her termination was wrongful and retaliatory, stemming from her refusal to engage in fraudulent activities she believed were taking place at the bank. She is seeking damages for wrongful termination and emotional distress. The State Bank defends against these claims, asserting that Ms. Smith was fired for poor performance and that the termination was unrelated to any allegations of fraud.

A group of crows is called a murder.
